Preprocessing pipelines

Source: R/harmonise-prep.R
mt_prep.Rd

mt_prep() bundles preprocessing steps that are applied to the data before a model is fitted. Because the steps are part of the fit, a backtest (mt_backtest()) re-runs them on every training window, so that ungrouping or smoothing never sees data after the forecast origin.

Usage

mt_prep(...)

step_ungroup(...)

step_smooth(...)

step_regroup(age = NULL, period = NULL)

step_grid(age = NULL, period = NULL)

step_window(years)

step_shocks(periods, action = c("interpolate", "exclude"))

mt_prep_apply(prep, data)

Arguments

...

Steps, applied in order.

age, period

Axes for step_regroup() and step_grid().

years

Number of most recent training years kept by step_window().

periods

Calendar years affected by a shock.

action

"interpolate" or "exclude".

prep

An mt_prep object or NULL (no preprocessing).

data

An mt_data object.

Value

An object of class mt_prep; mt_prep_apply() returns the processed mt_data object.

Details

Steps:

  • step_ungroup(...): mt_ungroup(), by default the published PCLM without rescaling to the group totals (models fitted to the ungrouped data and backtest scores against the grouped test data do not need exact group totals); step_ungroup(preserve_totals = TRUE) rescales;

  • step_smooth(...): mt_smooth(). The model is fitted to the smoothed rates; residuals and observation noise refer to the raw deaths. Smoothing over time (along = "period", or dims = 2) narrows the forecast intervals of models with a period index, so check coverage in a backtest and consider recalibrated();

  • step_regroup(age, period): mt_regroup();

  • step_grid(age, period): mt_set_grid();

  • step_window(years): keeps the last years years of the training data, a fitting period chosen relative to the forecast origin (for example after a change of trend; compare windows with tuned() or mt_backtest());

  • step_shocks(periods, action): periods with exceptional mortality (for example 2020-2022) are either replaced by log-linear interpolation of the rates of the neighbouring periods ("interpolate", deaths become exposure times the interpolated rate, provenance "interpolated") or removed ("exclude", only at the start or end of the data). With "interpolate", shock periods at the start or end of the data, which have no neighbour on one side, are removed instead, with a warning of class mt_warning_prep (as in a backtest whose training window ends inside the shock). The interpolated years enter the fit as if they had been observed: the model sees a straight line in the log rates between the neighbouring years, without the year-to-year variation of observed years. Models that estimate their uncertainty from year-to-year changes (for example the random walk of a period index) therefore estimate a smaller variance, and their forecast intervals become narrower; check coverage in a backtest. Excluding the periods (only possible at the edges) avoids this.

Examples

prep <- mt_prep(step_ungroup(), step_shocks(2005, action = "interpolate"))
prep
#> <mt_prep> 2 step(s)
#>   step_ungroup()
#>   step_shocks(periods=2005, action=interpolate)
x <- mt_prep_apply(prep, mt_example(years = 2001:2008))
